label: <DEL> step, when the sequence opens with tokens from {3,r,o,p,z,x,s,t,f,c,2,l}
explanation: Mostly a delimiter-step unit: 72% of activation mass is at the <DEL> step (41% of <DEL> steps fire, 8.2x lift), and the largest activations (top examples ~0.3) are all at <DEL>. Whether it fires at <DEL> depends on the first original tokens: rates are highest when first_tok (or orig(1)) is 3, r, o, p, z, x, s, t (first_tok=3 is the strongest), i.e. when the token about to be output first comes from this set. The other ~27% of mass is a ramp over the late original phase (t>=4, rising toward <DEL>, higher in longer sequences), almost only on first occurrences of a token (in_first=1 holds 96% of mass), and again in the same sequences, so it looks like a build-up that peaks at <DEL>. It never fires at t<3 and almost never in the copy phase (0.4% of mass). The predicate covers only <DEL>; the first-token set is a soft tendency, not a sharp rule (precision ~0.6), and adding the late original-phase ramp raised mass recall (0.79) but lowered F1.
